blocks.content: The National Green Tribunal provides a specialized forum for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established in 2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act for expeditious disposal of environmental disputes.
India is the third country globally—and the first developing nation—to establish a specialized environmental tribunal.
The tribunal is guided by the principles of natural justice and is not bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
NGT is mandated to dispose of applications and appeals within 6 months of filing.
The Principal Bench is located in New Delhi, supported by four zonal benches in Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, and Chennai.
NGT lacks jurisdiction over the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006.
Appeals against NGT orders can be filed directly before the Supreme Court within 90 days.
NGT decisions are bound by the Precautionary Principle, the Polluter Pays Principle, and the Sustainable Development Principle.
